sound: Checked: knownCompanyOf/namesakeOrgs (Mercury Records, Mercury Public Affairs and Nikola Tesla Institute all rejected); LittleSis company lookup (no orgs[0] fallback, 'likely' cap, typed company not in grade text, honest notes); Semantic Scholar grades on affiliations and homepage only; GitHub, Stack Overflow and S2 self-described caps; GitHub links followed only for established accounts or company org/domain; OpenAlex and ORCID hold(); own Bluesky posts kept out of red flags; Open Library and HF org prefixes (reproduced: possible); podcasts at most likely; ORCID never reads /person.

findings.title: Company-article trust check pastes the company name back in through 'the company', so a namesake's co-workers become trusted associates
findings.evidence: Ran wikipediaConnector with a 'Mercury (company)' article about a 1960s record label. The text says 'Jane Doe became the company's managing director'. The result was associate Robert Vance with trusted:true. With 'its' instead of 'the company's', trusted:false.
findings.scenario: Subject Jane Doe of fintech Mercury. The en-wiki article 'Mercury (company)' is about an older label and says 'Jane Doe became the company's managing director, working alongside co-founder Robert Vance'. pairsPersonWithCompany rewrites 'the company' as 'Mercury', and the grade comes back confirmed on the company. Vance becomes a trusted associate of the founder. This is the namesake injection the audit's knowledge-wp-company-trust fix was meant to remove.
findings.fix: Do not rewrite 'the company/firm/startup' to the article title. Require a sentence that names the person and the company by name, or a pronoun run that starts from one. For an ordinary-word company, also require the article lead to match a known fact (founding year, domain, a co-founder) before any thread is trusted.
findings.verifyNote: In code: pairsPersonWithCompany rewrites 'the company/firm/startup/business' as the article title, which companyArticle guarantees equals the typed company. This puts back the injection the audit removed: a namesake's 'the company's director' sentence makes associates trusted. Lowered to medium because a same-named article that writes 'Mercury' outright would pass anyway; the deeper gap is that a same-named company article is never checked against known facts.
findings.betterFix: Drop the rewrite: require a sentence that names the person and the company, or the pronoun run that follows one. In addition, before trusting any thread from a company article (always for an ordinary-word company name), require the article to match a known fact: domain, founding year, or a known co-founder or person anchor.

findings.title: profile.js never reads the structured data the sources now write, and reads Wikidata only when it is 'confirmed'
findings.evidence: buildProfile on Wikidata education and career records graded 'likely' with data.education and data.employers returned edu:[] and roles:[]. The same records marked 'confirmed' filled both. grep: no reader of data.employers, data.founded, data.positions, data.awards, secCik or scholarIds outside the sources.
findings.scenario: api-phase2.json published data.education, employers, positions, awards, founded, boards and memberships as fields the profile reads. buildProfile reads none of them. It reads Wikidata only when match==='confirmed', parsing the quote, which is clipped at 700 characters. A Wikidata entry graded 'likely' (resolved by school, or by the article) adds no school or job. A defended OpenAlex dissertation's data.education is ignored. The SEC CIK from Wikidata reaches no SEC source.
findings.fix: In buildProfile pass 1, for tied records (confirmed or likely) of any source, read data.education, data.employers, data.positions, data.founded, data.boards and data.awards directly (basis 'record'). Keep quote parsing only as a fallback. Pass identity data.secCik to the SEC connectors, or drop the field.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced. buildProfile reads Wikidata only when match==='confirmed' (by parsing the quote), and pass 2 skips Wikidata entirely. A 'likely' Wikidata education record with data.education, and an OpenAlex dissertation's data.education, both gave empty education. The secCik part is refuted: sec.js:1374 reads data.secCik.
findings.betterFix: In pass 1, for every tied record (confirmed or likely), read data.education, employers, positions, founded, boards, awards and memberships directly with basis 'record'. Keep quote parsing only as a fallback for confirmed Wikidata records. Add a test that a likely Wikidata record and an OpenAlex dissertation fill the résumé.

findings.title: A Wikidata entry resolved through the Wikipedia article still grades every record 'possible (name only)'; a lead that uses only the surname drops the person
findings.evidence: Mocked one candidate with an empty employer list and an article that names Acme Robotics. Identity, education and career all came back 'possible', 'matched by name only'; threads untrusted; profile empty. A lead of 'Quenneville is the co-founder ... of Acme Robotics' gave 'nothing in that record mentions Acme Robotics. None was used.'
findings.scenario: Case 1: the founder's only Wikidata entry omits the startup and the article names it, so findEntity resolves by 'context' via 'article'. wdFinding grades on entityContext, which lacks the company, so every record is 'possible' and threads stay untrusted. Family is still read, because by==='context'. Case 2: if the company appears only in a surname sentence (the usual Wikipedia style), articleNamesCompany fails. withFullName is not applied, so the true entry is dropped.
findings.fix: Keep the matching article sentence on the entity (entity.evidence) and add it to entityContext, so the grade sees the company. Cap these records at 'likely' with the reason 'the Wikipedia article names the company'. In articleNamesCompany, apply withFullName as well as withPronouns. Carry `via` onto the entity.
findings.verifyNote: In code: findEntity returns {by:'context', via:'article'}, but run() builds entity = {...found.entity, by}, so via is dropped. entityContext holds no company, so every record grades as name-only 'possible' while family is still read. articleNamesCompany applies withPronouns but not withFullName, so a lead that gives only the surname fails.
findings.betterFix: Store the matching article sentence on the entity and add it to the grading context, with the identity record capped at 'likely' and the reason that the Wikipedia article names the company. In articleNamesCompany, apply withFullName before withPronouns; this is safe because the article is about the single candidate.

findings.title: A thesis still in preparation appears in the résumé as a held doctorate
findings.evidence: buildProfile on a theses.fr record with data { degree:'Doctorat', defended:false, institution:'Université Paris-Saclay' } produced education [{school:'Université Paris-Saclay', degree:'Doctorat', to:null}].
findings.scenario: scholar.js writes data.education only for defended theses, with the comment 'a thesis in preparation is no degree yet'. profile.js ignores that field and reads d.institution and d.degree. theses.fr sets degree 'Doctorat' for every thesis, finished or not. An investor sees a PhD the person does not hold. A defended OpenAlex dissertation (source 'publications') is not read at all.
findings.fix: In profile.js, read academic-record and publications education from data.education only, which scholar.js already restricts to defended theses. If kept, mark a registered thesis as 'doctoral candidate'. Remove the `d.institution && d.degree` branch.
findings.verifyNote: Reproduced. A theses.fr record with defended:false and degree 'Doctorat' (scholar.js:627 sets that degree for every thesis) produced education {school, degree:'Doctorat', to:null} through the `d.institution && d.degree` branch at profile.js:629. That branch ignores the defended-only data.education.
findings.betterFix: Remove the d.institution/d.degree branch and read data.education, which scholar.js limits to defended theses. If a registered thesis is shown at all, show it as 'Doctoral candidate' and never as a degree held.

findings.title: Hugging Face grades an account 'likely' when only the same handle and the name match
findings.evidence: huggingFaceConnector.run with a handle task 'janedoe' (platform 'x') and an HF account 'janedoe' stating 'Jane Doe' returned match 'likely' with no company, link or domain.
findings.scenario: Founder Jane Doe's X handle is 'janedoe'. An unrelated Hugging Face user 'janedoe' who also wrote 'Jane Doe' is graded 'likely'. The handle is just the name, so nothing beyond the name ties the account. presence.js's own rule for the same case (gradeReached, not exact) falls back to grading the text, which gives name-only 'possible'.
findings.fix: In hfGrade, treat 'reached' as a tie only when exact (an HF link or an HF handle). For the same handle on another service, require a known company in the account's organisations or bio, or a link back to a known domain or handle. Otherwise 'possible' with 'name match only, verify identity'.
findings.verifyNote: In code: hfGrade gives 'likely' whenever `reached` is non-empty, including when the same handle is found on another service (presenceMore.js:243-246). presence.js gradeReached grades that same case on the text alone, which gives 'possible' with only the name, or 'likely' only with a link back. When the handle is just the name, this is a name-only tie shown as 'likely'.
findings.betterFix: Pass exact into hfGrade. When the account was not reached exactly, require a known company in its organisations or bio, or a link to a known domain or another handle, before grading 'likely'. Otherwise grade 'possible' (name match only), the same rule as presence.js gradeReached.
